claim: A deterministic finite-state machine extracted from an agent's past execution traces can condition next-action/skill prediction, cutting cross-entropy by 21% (0.155 bits) versus identical methods conditioning on raw context without FSM state.
stance_target: probabilistic skill-sequence prediction from agent-trace history is a tractable, measurable capability
scope_conditions: 12 public agent-trace datasets (SWE-agent, WebArena, AgentNet, tau2-bench, ATBench, OSWorld, SWE-smith) across 8 agent domains
quoted_support: FSM state conditioning provides +0.155 bits mean / +0.136 bits median (21%) over raw context alone (FSM-AD: 0.580 vs. Pure-AD: 0.735 CE), positive on all 6 datasets.

claim: A minimal FSM-derived prompt format (next-action probabilities + top-15 multi-step continuations from the current state) beats Agent Workflow Memory on LLM-judged next-action top-1 accuracy on all 8 tested datasets, with gains ranging +0.8pp to +25.3pp.
stance_target: structural memory derived from trace history outperforms linear workflow-memory baselines for skill-chaining prediction
scope_conditions: LLM judge gpt-4.1-mini; 8 datasets including WebArena, SWE-smith, SWE-agent, tau2-bench variants, ATBench, OSWorld
quoted_support: the FSM beats AWM on all eight datasets (Table 4), with gains ranging from +0.8pp (tau2-bench airline) to +25.3pp (SWE-smith).

claim: Verbose context formats that enumerate full FSM state/transition structure underperform a minimal probabilistic next-action format, showing that probabilistic skill-sequence predictions must be presented sparsely to the LLM, not as exhaustive graphs.
stance_target: design constraint for implementing probabilistic sequencing systems: minimal, probability-ranked context beats verbose structural dumps
scope_conditions: tau2-bench retail dataset, N=1,095 traces, gpt-4.1-mini judge
quoted_support: The verbose "state + transitions + full structure" format (ASG-full, 52.2%) underperforms AWM (52.9%) because listing every state and transition drowns the next-step signal... The minimal format... wins at 65.1% (+12.9pp over AWM and +12.9pp over ASG-full).

claim: Per-state behavioral and cross-entropy anomaly features derived from the trace-history FSM predict task failure with held-out AUROC up to 0.941, enabling early stopping at 32% of trace completion while saving 68% of remaining compute on SWE-agent.
stance_target: trace-history-derived structural models enable predictive, compute-saving runtime intervention
scope_conditions: 9 labeled real/synthetic agent-trace datasets; SWE-agent early-stopping monitor specifically
quoted_support: FSM cross-entropy anomaly features reach up to 0.941 held-out AUROC (tau2-bench telecom, 43 states)... triggers early-stopping at 32% mean trace completion on SWE-agent (precision 85.9%, recall 95.5%, saving 68% of remaining compute).

claim: Behavioral FSM topology extracted from agent traces is largely model-invariant: a single FSM built from four different LLMs' traces on tau2-bench achieves 1.000 replay fitness on each model individually, with an 80-92% shared dominant transition backbone.
stance_target: skill-sequence structure is a property of the deployment harness/toolset rather than the underlying model, implying a single probabilistic-sequencing model can generalize across agent/model swaps
scope_conditions: tau2-bench (airline, retail, telecom) across 4 chat models
quoted_support: FSMs also transfer across models: a single FSM built from all four LLMs' traces achieves 1.000 fitness on each model individually (per-model FSMs share a near-identical state vocabulary and a dominant 80-92% transition backbone, indicating largely model-invariant topology).

claim: The FSM extraction method is deterministic and hyperparameter-free, constructing automata in 1-110ms versus 7,000-36,000ms for the RPNI grammatical-inference baseline, a 328-10,611x speedup, enabling real-time production monitoring.
stance_target: probabilistic skill-sequence models can be built and updated cheaply enough for real-time production use
quoted_support: Our method constructs FSMs in 1-110 ms across all datasets, compared to 7,000-36,000 ms for RPNI (328-10,611x speedup). Per-trace replay completes in 0.003-0.015 ms, enabling real-time monitoring of production agent systems.

claim: The extracted FSM only captures the directly-follows closure of observed traces, not the agent's true generating language, and is provably impossible to fully identify from positive examples alone (Gold's 1967 theorem), so adversarial traces preserving activity bigram statistics can bypass it.
stance_target: claims that trace-derived probabilistic sequencing models provide complete or adversarially-robust behavioral guarantees
scope_conditions: general limitation of positive-only automata learning
quoted_support: The FSM accepts the directly-follows closure of the observed traces, not the agent's generating language; adversarial traces preserving activity bigram statistics can replay.

claim: Conditioning on current FSM state reduces entropy by 51-80% versus unconditioned activity frequencies, explaining why compact state spaces (7-43 states) suffice to capture agent skill-sequencing structure.
stance_target: agent behavior exhibits strong enough sequential regularity that compact probabilistic models can predict skill sequences effectively
quoted_support: agent activity sequences exhibit strong sequential regularity: conditioning on the previous symbol reduces entropy by 51-80%.
